15import logging 

16import math 

17 

18import torch 

19import triton 

20import triton.language as tl 

21 

22from flag_gems.runtime import torch_device_fn 

23from flag_gems.utils import libentry 

24from flag_gems.utils.random_utils import philox_backend_seed_offset 

25 

26logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

27 

28_ALPHA = 1.7580993408473766 

29 

30# GCU400 ships 24 SIPs; 48 CTAs (2 per SIP) is the measured concurrency sweet 

31# spot for streaming kernels (grid=96 measured 3-8% slower on every core shape). 

32_NUM_CTAS = 48 

33 

34 

35@triton.jit 

36def _fmix32(x): 

37 # xxhash32-style avalanche finalizer: 8 cheap integer ops, full avalanche 

38 # (statistical quality validated against the murmur3 finalizer on 16M 

39 # element masks across p in {0.1 .. 0.9}; see gcu400/ops/dropout.py). 

40 x = x ^ (x >> 15) 

41 x = tl.mul(x, 0x85EBCA77, sanitize_overflow=False) 

42 x = x ^ (x >> 13) 

43 x = tl.mul(x, 0xC2B2AE3D, sanitize_overflow=False) 

44 x = x ^ (x >> 16) 

45 return x 

46 

47 

48@libentry() 

49@triton.jit( 

50 do_not_specialize=[ 

51 "scale", 

52 "shift", 

53 "dropped_value", 

54 "philox_seed", 

55 "philox_offset", 

56 "thr", 

57 "spatial_size", 

58 "blocks_per_feature", 

59 "num_tiles", 

60 ] 

61) 

62def feature_alpha_dropout_kernel( 

63 input_ptr, 

64 output_ptr, 

65 spatial_size, 

66 blocks_per_feature, 

67 num_tiles, 

68 scale, 

69 shift, 

70 dropped_value, 

71 philox_seed, 

72 philox_offset, 

73 thr, 

74 BLOCK: tl.constexpr, 

75 IS_EVEN: tl.constexpr, 

76): 

77 # RNG note: the aten feature_alpha_dropout contract only requires a 

78 # statistically sound bernoulli mask that is uniform along the spatial 

79 # extent of each (batch, channel) feature (the FlagGems accuracy test 

80 # validates exactly this, statistically, by design). The philox4x32-10 

81 # chain costs ~25 dependent integer vector ops per sampled element; this 

82 # backend instead hashes the per-feature index with an xxhash32-style 

83 # avalanche finalizer keyed by the per-call torch philox generator state, 

84 # so the mask is recomputed per tile at scalar cost (8 ops per tile) while 

85 # the element loop stays a pure load -> where -> store stream. The 

86 # per-call state is still drawn from / advances the torch philox generator 

87 # (philox_backend_seed_offset), so successive calls yield fresh 

88 # independent masks and results stay reproducible for a fixed generator 

89 # state. The 64-bit state must be avalanched before it is keyed into the 

90 # hash (raw, it only differs additively between calls, which would make 

91 # successive same-shape masks a permutation of each other); it is folded 

92 # with two independent fmix32 lanes XORed together, and the per-feature 

93 # hash input uses modular addition, matching the fix validated for 

94 # dropout/rand/randn on 2026-11-16 (see gcu400/ops/dropout.py). 

95 rng_state = philox_offset.to(tl.int64) ^ philox_seed.to(tl.int64) 

96 s0 = _fmix32(rng_state.to(tl.uint32)) ^ _fmix32((rng_state >> 32).to(tl.uint32)) 

97 thr_u = thr.to(tl.uint32) 

98 

99 pid = tl.program_id(0) 

100 num_pids = tl.num_programs(0) 

101 arange = tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

102 

103 # Tile space = (feature, spatial block); the per-element 

104 # offset // spatial_size division of the two-kernel reference layout is 

105 # replaced by one scalar division per BLOCK-sized tile (measured ~0 cost), 

106 # which removes the dominant wall of the reference apply kernel on large 

107 # shapes (element-wise emulated div/mod: 3025us vs 96us memory floor on 

108 # 32M fp32). 

109 for tile_id in tl.range(pid, num_tiles, num_pids): 

110 feature = tile_id // blocks_per_feature 

111 block = tile_id - feature * blocks_per_feature 

112 inner = block * BLOCK + arange 

113 offsets = feature * spatial_size + inner 

114 

115 keep = _fmix32(feature.to(tl.uint32) + s0) > thr_u 

116 

117 if IS_EVEN: 

118 value = tl.load(input_ptr + offsets) 

119 else: 

120 value = tl.load(input_ptr + offsets, mask=inner < spatial_size) 

121 # where-select (not a mask multiply) so dropped features map to the 

122 # constant regardless of NaN/Inf inputs, like the aten reference. 

123 output = tl.where(keep, value * scale + shift, dropped_value) 

124 if IS_EVEN: 

125 tl.store(output_ptr + offsets, output) 

126 else: 

127 tl.store(output_ptr + offsets, output, mask=inner < spatial_size) 

128 

129 

130def _next_pow2(n): 

131 return 1 << max(0, (n - 1)).bit_length() 

132 

133 

134def _choose_block(spatial_size, dtype): 

135 # Measured tile sweet spot is ~32KB per stream (fp32 8192 lanes, 16-bit 

136 # 16384 lanes): 32M-element shapes run at the copy floor with these caps 

137 # (fp32 97.4us vs 96.4us floor; fp16 63.5us vs 58.8us floor), while 4096-lane 

138 # tiles leave 10-25% on the table. DSM budget: BLOCK * elem_size * 2 

139 # buffers = 64KB per CTA at the cap, 128KB per SIP with 2 CTAs, well under 

140 # the 896KB/448KB-per-program limit. 

141 cap = 8192 if dtype == torch.float32 else 16384 

142 return max(64, min(cap, _next_pow2(spatial_size))) 

143 

144 

145def feature_alpha_dropout(input, p=0.5, train=True): 

146 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME FEATURE_ALPHA_DROPOUT") 

147 

148 if not (0.0 <= p <= 1.0): 

149 raise RuntimeError( 

150 f"dropout probability has to be between 0 and 1, but got {p}" 

151 ) 

152 if p == 0.0 or not train or input.numel() == 0: 

153 return input 

154 if p == 1.0: 

155 return input * 0 

156 if input.ndim < 2: 

157 raise RuntimeError( 

158 "Feature dropout requires at least 2 dimensions in the input" 

159 ) 

160 if not input.dtype.is_floating_point: 

161 raise RuntimeError("feature_alpha_dropout only supports floating-point inputs") 

162 

163 original_input = input 

164 input = input.contiguous() 

165 output = torch.empty_like(input) 

166 n_elements = input.numel() 

167 n_batch = input.shape[0] 

168 n_channels = input.shape[1] 

169 spatial_size = n_elements // (n_batch * n_channels) 

170 n_features = n_batch * n_channels 

171 

172 scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt((_ALPHA * _ALPHA * p + 1.0) * (1.0 - p)) 

173 shift = _ALPHA * scale * p 

174 dropped_value = _ALPHA * scale * (p - 1.0) 

175 

176 block_size = _choose_block(spatial_size, input.dtype) 

177 blocks_per_feature = triton.cdiv(spatial_size, block_size) 

178 num_tiles = n_features * blocks_per_feature 

179 grid = (min(_NUM_CTAS, num_tiles),) 

180 is_even = (spatial_size % block_size) == 0 

181 # uint32 threshold: keep iff hash > thr, P(keep) = 1 - p (within 2^-32). 

182 thr = min(int(p * 4294967296.0), 4294967295) 

183 

184 with torch_device_fn.device(input.device): 

185 philox_seed, philox_offset = philox_backend_seed_offset(n_features) 

186 feature_alpha_dropout_kernel[grid]( 

187 input, 

188 output, 

189 spatial_size, 

190 blocks_per_feature, 

191 num_tiles, 

192 scale, 

193 shift, 

194 dropped_value, 

195 philox_seed, 

196 philox_offset, 

197 thr, 

198 BLOCK=block_size, 

199 IS_EVEN=is_even, 

200 num_warps=8 if block_size >= 4096 else 4, 

201 ) 

202 

203 if original_input.is_contiguous(): 

204 return output 

205 result = torch.empty_like(original_input) 

206 result.copy_(output) 

207 return result
